topics.title: Introduction and Key Considerations
topics.objective: The candidate will understand the key considerations for and key concepts underlying general insurance actuarial work.

outcomes.text: Identify sources of professionalism requirements and good practice
Demonstrate knowledge of good practice related to actuarial work
Use the actuarial control cycle to frame actuarial work
Understand the components of ultimate values
Explain how estimates of ultimate values are used
Demonstrate the importance of understanding key terminology and interrelationships
Identify different types of data used for actuarial work
Explain the responsibilities of the actuary related to data
Describe how and why data are segregated and aggregated
Describe qualitative information required for actuarial work
Understand the sources of data and information for actuarial work
Understand credibility as used for actuarial work
Explain the application of trend adjustments in actuarial work
Illustrate the types of trend that influence the future cost of claims, expenses, and premiums
Identify the actuary’s responsibilities with regards to documentation for actuarial work
Describe the role of professional judgment in actuarial work

resources.citation: Fundamentals of General Insurance Actuarial Analysis, J. Friedland, 2nd Edition, 2022
Actuarial Standards of Practice, Actuarial Standards Board of the American Academy of Actuaries, No. 25, Credibility Procedures, 2013

topics.title: Preparing Claims and Exposure Data for Actuarial Work
topics.objective: The candidate will demonstrate the ability to prepare claims and exposure data for general insurance actuarial work.

outcomes.text: Create development triangles of claims and counts from detailed claim transaction data
Describe the different types of exposures used for conducting actuarial work
Calculate written, earned, in-force and unearned premiums for portfolios of policies with various policy terms and earnings patterns
Adjust historical earned premiums to current rate levels
Understand types of changes influencing average premium levels
Describe adjustments needed to estimate ultimate premiums

resources.citation: Fundamentals of General Insurance Actuarial Analysis, J. Friedland, 2nd Edition, 2022

parts.text: Appendices A through C and F (excluding Sections A.3.6, A.5)

topics.title: Projecting Ultimate Claims
topics.objective: The candidate will know how to calculate and evaluate projected ultimate values.

outcomes.text: Identify considerations for selecting methods for estimating ultimate claims
Identify and describe good practice related to projecting ultimate claims with regard to required data, large claims, and comparison of current to prior actuarial work
Identify the types of development triangles that can be used for investigative testing
Analyze development triangles for investigative testing

Describe the key assumptions underlying the following projection methods: development method, development-based frequency-severity method, expected method, Bornhuetter Ferguson method, Benktander method, Cape Cod method, and Generalized Cape Cod method
Demonstrate knowledge of good practice related to projecting ultimate values
Estimate ultimate values using the methods cited in (e)
Describe the Berquist-Sherman data adjustments and their key assumptions
Adjust data triangles for changes in the adequacy of case estimates or changes in the rate of claim settlement using a Berquist-Sherman data adjustment
Estimate ultimate claims using the appropriate Berquist-Sherman data adjustments
Explain the effect of changing conditions on the projection methods cited in (e)
Assess the appropriateness of the projection methods cited in (e) in varying circumstances
Evaluate and justify selections of ultimate values based on the methods cited in (e)

resources.citation: Fundamentals of General Insurance Actuarial Analysis, J. Friedland, 2nd Edition, 2022

parts.text: Part 4: Basic Methods for Estimating Ultimate Claims (excluding 15.8, 16.6, 16.7, 17.8, 18.8, 19.6, 20.6, 21.3.5, and 21.3.6)
Appendices A through C and F (excluding A.3.6 and A.5)

topics.title: Financial Reporting
topics.objective: The candidate will understand financial reporting of claim liabilities with respect to unpaid unallocated loss adjustment expenses.

outcomes.text: Describe the key assumptions underlying ratio and count-based methods for estimating unpaid unallocated loss adjustment expenses
Estimate unpaid unallocated loss adjustment expenses using ratio and count-based methods
Evaluate and justify selections of unpaid unallocated loss adjustment expenses based on ratio and count-based methods

resources.citation: Fundamentals of General Insurance Actuarial Analysis, J. Friedland, 2nd Edition, 2022

topics.title: Trending
topics.objective: The candidate will understand trending procedures as applied to ultimate claims, exposures and premiums.

outcomes.text: Identify and describe the influences of portfolio changes on claim frequency and severity
Identify the time periods associated with trending procedures
Analyze and evaluate trend for claims (including frequency, severity, and pure premium) and exposures (including inflation-sensitive exposures and premiums)
Choose trend rates for claims (frequency, severity, and pure premium) and exposures
Calculate trend factors for claims and exposures

resources.citation: Fundamentals of General Insurance Actuarial Analysis, J. Friedland, 2nd Edition, 2022

parts.text: Appendices A through C, and F (excluding A.3.6, A.5)

topics.title: Ratemaking
topics.objective: The candidate will understand how to apply the fundamental ratemaking techniques of general insurance.

outcomes.text: Quantify different types of expenses required for ratemaking including expense trending procedures
Incorporate underwriting profit and contingency margins in ratemaking
Explain the requirements for loadings for catastrophes and large claims in ratemaking
Calculate loadings for catastrophes and large claims
Apply loadings for catastrophes and large claims in ratemaking
Describe the claim ratio and pure premium methods of ratemaking
Calculate indicated rates and rate changes using the claim ratio and pure premium methods
Demonstrate the use of credibility in ratemaking

topics.objective: The candidate will be able to define an approach for actuarial analyses supporting financial reporting and ratemaking analyses under various real-life scenarios. The candidates will be able to define funding requirements for self-insurers.

outcomes.text: Identify data and information requirements
Conduct investigative testing
Choose projection methods to estimate ultimate values
Estimate ultimate values
Justify selections of ultimate values
Develop reserves for financial reporting
